admissions.reproduction: Six literal-separator variants accepted by native Hadolint lose command bytes in the baseline projection; six comments can introduce fake SHELL instructions. BuildKit scanner splits only on LF.
admissions.owner: devops_programs Docker adapter before workflow-embedded-program and workflow-shell-format
admissions.gap: str.splitlines uses boundaries outside Docker grammar; neither upstream tool can lint source omitted or assigned the wrong interpreter by the adapter.
admissions.noChangeHarm: Literal separator data is truncated and comments can select an interpreter that Docker never selects, losing formatter coverage and misclassifying embedded programs.
admissions.invalidState: Incomplete or misclassified executable source, not a source-style preference.
admissions.smallestFix: Use Docker physical LF lines and canonical SourceDocument coordinates; share the existing Make coordinate translation where contracts match.

admissions.reproduction: AST-normalized helpers are identical: 20-line __all__ mention predicate in two selected rules and 9-line test collection generator in two other selected rules.
admissions.owner: Python lint engine shared export and pytest helper boundaries
admissions.gap: Four private implementations repeat two contracts; existing TestProvenance function selection intentionally differs and cannot replace pytest collection.
admissions.noChangeHarm: Maintaining duplicate predicates and generators repeats the same implementation in four locations.
admissions.invalidState: Implementation consolidation only; no new prohibited program state or user policy.
admissions.smallestFix: Share the pure helper functions, preserve caller exclusions and ordering, compare full diagnostics and measured combined checks. Avoid cache or broader collection semantics.

reproductionCommands: code-standards --root . maintain rules changes --before origin/main --after HEAD
limitations: This is a reproducible machine-assisted source/test review with native examples. Deep manual and adversarial analysis focuses on admitted candidates; it is not exhaustive manual review of every selected rule.
300 draws cover 200 distinct rules; repeated draws reuse evidence and are not independent semantic coverage.
The 30 shell passes include related syntax variants; pass count does not represent 30 independent defects.
Only already-local repositories were scanned. Python selection takes the first 250 sorted eligible tracked paths per root after exclusions, rather than an unbiased whole-repository sample.

Five retained Python findings were compared by full tuple and structurally inspected; user intent and pre-existing false positives were not inferred. The seeded corpus separately verifies seven positives and seven negatives.
One pre-existing native formatter failure remains in the shell corpus. Native aggregate findings and formatter outcomes are unchanged.
Hadolint does not accept these heredoc fixtures; heredoc checks instead compare projection and harmless native shell execution. This fixture-owner correction was applied to both phases.
Docker ShellCheck diagnostics remain owned by Hadolint. Adapter finding-anchor regressions use the native shfmt result, which reports a position rather than a region.
Docker LF instruction coordinates and bare CR data map to canonical SourceDocument editor coordinates. Existing Make source and diagnostics retain their contracts.
Pure helper sharing is a maintenance improvement. Combined measured checks are approximately neutral; no universal speed improvement is claimed.

Docker projection is neutral on the 200-instruction LF fixture, about 1.7 percent slower on its CRLF variant, and about 0.9 microseconds slower on the three-instruction fixture. These adapter timings exclude native subprocess cost.
Private identities, source pins, paths, hashes, snippets and complete findings stay in owner-readable overlays; this report includes only public rule data and redacted aggregates.

The final integration benchmark compares unchanged helper copies from the concurrent main revision with the rebased helpers. Initial source selections, corpus revisions, findings and measurements retain their original audit baseline.

integration.reason: Concurrent main merge changed the release baseline after the first exact-head checks passed. Audit selection and corpus pins retain the original baseline; no source pin was refreshed.
